page: Amazon Web Services c8g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU architecture is arm64, with no hyperthreading enabled. It includes a cache configuration of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block read-only and write-only memory bandwidth benchmarks both rank in the top 25%, reaching 302.31 GB/sec and 123.66 GB/sec respectively. Computational performance is also strong in multi-threaded environments, as evidenced by top 25% results in Geekbench single-core (1888.0) and multi-core (15991.0) tests, as well as bzip3 decompression. However, the hardware exhibits a performance tradeoff in complex AI workloads, with prompt processing for medium-sized (7B) language models falling into the bottom 25% at 31.15 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer a high density of physical compute resources relative to memory capacity. This makes the instance suitable for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated core execution without requiring local storage. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data decompression, text processing, database operations, and software compilation. It is less suited for large-scale LLM inference or workloads requiring local NVMe storage.
